target_customer: Car owners wanting repairs at home or work, later fleets, insurers and B2B partners
problem: Car owners found repair shops inconvenient and opaque on price; the founders claimed 80 percent of repairs did not need a shop.
business_model: Marketplace connecting car owners with independent mobile mechanics, with a take rate on labor and a fee on parts; later B2B products

founders.name: Art Agrawal
founders.background_notes: Presented at TechCrunch Disrupt SF 2012; full name given as Abhas Art Agrawal in coverage.

competitors.name: Jiffy Lube
competitors.what: Quick-lube chain and shop network for routine maintenance
competitors.traction_then: National chain; said its average conventional oil change was $37

technical_complexity.rationale: Instant pricing engine over vehicle and repair data, scheduling and mechanic vetting; mostly marketplace engineering with a data-heavy pricing component.

defensibility.rationale: Mechanic supply and a pricing dataset gave some edge, but mechanics could work for rivals and Wikipedia notes later quality and safety problems.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not copy it directly; Wrench, a mobile repair rival, acquired it in June 2022.

market_need_then: The company claimed a $120B annual market for basic repair on out-of-warranty, non-luxury cars and 30 to 50 percent savings over shops; it had 10 mechanics at launch and won TechCrunch Disrupt SF 2012.

branding.domain_note: yourmechanic.com is the company domain; the legal entity is Wrench, Inc., dba YourMechanic.

identity.voice_and_tone: Transparent, trust-centred messaging: total trust comes from total transparency

branding.brand_signature: We come to you car repair; 2012 TechCrunch Disrupt SF winner
branding.community_and_virality: Featured in NYT, Forbes and Inc. per its site; the name was registered as a trademark in 2016 (first use September 12, 2012). No merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: A Disrupt win and national press, plus a descriptive name that told customers the offer, but a generic name with limited ownable identity.

pivots.to: Added a suite of business-to-business products
pivots.why: Stated on the company description; reason not sourced

outcome_analysis: YourMechanic won TechCrunch Disrupt SF in 2012, raised a $1.8M seed and a $24M round in 2016, and grew to over 100 staff and hundreds of mechanics, reaching a June 2022 acquisition by Wrench with undisclosed terms. Wikipedia attributes a later decline to a late-2016 CEO change, lawsuits and safety issues, but that account rests on one source, so the cause of the soft exit is uncertain.
notes: The 2016 round is labeled Series B by Private Equity International; month varies (Wikipedia March, an aggregator February), so only the year is given. The prior $6M or so implied by the $32M total is unexplained and a Series A was not found. A 2018 round of about $10.2M (American Family, SoftBank, Verizon; total $42.2M) appears in a Global Venturing snippet only and is unverified, and the page was not opened. Acquisition date June 2022 (one source June 2, the Wrench post June 20). The Wikipedia infobox lists John Wall as CTO against Dongyi Liao in the history; the YC page lists Liao. Founder education and prior employers were not found in sources opened.
